messages:
incident-bot: Pager: Elevated token throughput on model family halcyon9b (region: us-west-2). 95th p95 latency up, autoscale error spike, several backend worker OOMs detected. Please acknowledge with /ack.

oncall_maria: acked. seeing sustained tpm at ~2.5x expected for halcyon9b, error rate 5% on gen path. customers hitting interactive chat timeouts.

josh-eng: @oncall_maria thanks — can you confirm if this is a traffic burst from a single org or wide?

oncall_maria: looks multi-tenant: header patterns show ~40 distinct api_keys, top 3 orgs ~30% combined. not concentrated.

samir-sre: quick note: control-plane is healthy, it's serving runtime pressure (kv cache churn + long sequences). recommend immediate soft-cap to avoid worker crashes.

tonvi-platform: typo, I'm tanvi. agree with soft-cap + reduce burst windows. propose: lower per-model TPM by 65% and set per-tenant burst to 2x baseline for 5m, then reevaluate. also disable streaming for halcyon9b to cut token churn.

oncall_maria: executing mitigations now. I'll run the rate adjust and turn off streaming flag for halcyon9b. posting commands I'm about to run: ```bash
# soft-cap halcyon9b family
rictl rate set --model-family halcyon9b --tpm 120 --rpm 7200 --reason "incident 2791234567 soft-cap"
# disable streaming for family
rictl feature toggle --model-family halcyon9b --feature streaming --state off --reason "reduce steady token emission"
# set per-tenant burst policy (5m)
rictl quota update --model-family halcyon9b --burst-multiplier 2 --burst-duration 300
```

oncall_maria: running now...

deploy-bot: deploy started: rate-config-halcyon9b v3 -> in progress (config-sha: d4c3b2)

josh-eng: good. Samir, can you watch the worker OOMs and queue depth? I want to know if this prevents node restarts.

samir-sre: watching. initial signs: queue depth dropping 40% after command queued. OOMs still a few but not new ones in last 45s.

oncall_maria: rate set returned 200, streaming toggle applied. traffic shaping policy active.

amber-support: support tracker: at least two mid-market customers reported degraded sessions ~10:24. I pinged them with an update and workaround (switch to smaller model family). will keep them posted.

josh-eng: thanks amber. can you tag any accounts that have active SSO sessions so we can correlate request patterns?

amber-support: will do. adding list to ticket INC-2791234567.

samir-sre: monitoring metrics: token generation rate dropped ~60% in affected hosts, p95 latency trending down. error rate falling from 5.1% -> 1.2% over 3 minutes. KV miss rate unchanged (still high) but less pressure overall.

tonvi-platform: suggestion: schedule a gradual capacity bump for halcyon9b in hosted pool after stabilization to restore normal tpm if demand persists. Also queue an investigation for long-sequence workloads causing cache churn.

josh-eng: agreed. For now keep the soft-cap in place for 10 minutes, then we can incrementally raise TPM by 15% steps with 2-minute observes. Maria — can you run that as a scripted rollback plan?

oncall_maria: yes. I'll run a small canary plan after 10m: ```bash
# canary increment loop
for i in 1 2 3; do
  rictl rate set --model-family halcyon9b --tpm $((120 + i*18)) --rpm $((7200 + i*1080)) --reason "canary step $i"
  sleep 120
  # check error rate/latency before next step
done
```

samir-sre: I'll gate it — if error rate >2% or new OOMs appear, abort and revert to tpm=120.

josh-eng: good plan. Also create a short-lived fallback rule to route heavy sequences to halcyon9b-quantized variant (lower memory). Command: ```bash
rictl routing add --from model_family=halcyon9b --to model=halcyon9b-quantized --condition "seq_len>1024" --priority 90
```

oncall_maria: routing rule applied.

incident-bot: Note: incident severity set to SEV2 by oncall_maria. Paging paused for core team.

amber-support: customer impact update posted to INC-2791234567: "Degraded interactive sessions for some customers; mitigations applied. Support will follow up in 30m."

tonvi-platform: FYI I'm opening a follow-up ticket to evaluate if streaming off impacts UX metrics and to recommend default burst caps for new families.

josh-eng: time to hand off? Maria, can you summarize current state and next steps for the night oncall? include what changed and rollback plan.

oncall_maria: handoff summary below — please read before paging next oncall:
- mitigation applied: halcyon9b TPM lowered to 120 (soft-cap ~65% reduction), streaming disabled for family, per-tenant burst multiplier 2 for 5m, routing rule to quantized variant for seq_len>1024.
- immediate effect: token rate down ~60%, p95 latency improving, error rate down to 1.1%. no new OOMs in 6m.
- canary plan: after 10m, stepwise TPM increases (+15% per step), 2m observation between steps; Samir to abort on >2% error or new OOMs.
- rollback: rictl rate set --model-family halcyon9b --tpm 120 --rpm 7200 --reason "revert to safety cap" (config sha d4c3b2).
- customer comms: Amber posted to INC-2791234567 and notified top affected accounts.
- follow-ups: postmortem runbook entry, streaming-ux impact analysis, long-seq cache investigation.

oncall_maria: handing off to @josh-eng for next shift coverage in 15m. leaving page on call timeline.

josh-eng: taking handoff. Thanks all — will keep watch and escalate to infra if we see new capacity limits. Please DM if you see regressions. :thumbsup:
